           Informational Report on Stakeholder Processes Addressing Resource Adequacy for New
           Large Loads

Dear Secretary Reese:

           As directed by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“Commission”) Order

Instituting Proceeding Under Section 206 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”) (“Show Cause

Order”),1 PJM submits this informational report to update the Commission on the current status of

proposals under consideration in the stakeholder process to address the issue of resource adequacy

to serve new large loads and other ongoing stakeholder processes that aim to increase the pace of

adding generating capacity in the PJM Region.

I.         INFORMATIONAL FILING

           PJM has been working proactively to address the issue of resource adequacy for new large

loads and to increase the pace of adding generating capacity in the PJM Region through myriad

stakeholder processes. As further explained below, this effort is most directly evidenced by the

Critical Issue Fast Path (“CIFP”) for the development of a reliability backstop procurement

(“RBP”) and a framework for service during periods of insufficient resource adequacy.2 These

             a. Stakeholder Processes Addressing Resource Adequacy to Serve New Large
                Loads
                      i. Reliability Backstop Procurement and Framework for Service During
                         Periods of Insufficient Resource Adequacy
        PJM has recently conducted a stakeholder process through a CIFP that directly addresses

the issue of resource adequacy to serve new large loads. Specifically, pursuant to the directive of

the PJM Board,4 PJM initiated a CIFP regarding the execution of an RBP and the implementation

of a framework for service during periods of insufficient resource adequacy.5 The CIFP for RBP

was convened to address the evolving risk profile in the PJM Region by developing a proposal to

address backstop procurement which specifies core award parameters, such as price, term, and

quantity, as well as cost allocation mechanisms to serve as a transitional measure towards

addressing resource adequacy concerns while options for a more durable mechanism are evaluated

as part of the broader market review.6

        The CIFP addressing service during periods of insufficient resource adequacy was

convened to focus on developing a solution to both incentivize investment in generation and

manage the reliability challenges during the transitional period in which new load additions are

outpacing the additions of new capacity in the PJM system. This framework will provide PJM

operators with a tool to maintain reliability while allowing all large loads to connect to the system.

Large loads that do not bring sufficient supply resources to the system to cover their requirements

should not negatively impact reliability for other load, and therefore these large loads may be

required to reduce their withdrawals from the transmission system before PJM needs to curtail

other load.7 Because these issues have linkage, the PJM Board moved to consolidate them into

one CIFP.8

        In total, 24 proposals were submitted for consideration by PJM, the Independent Market

Monitor for PJM, and various stakeholder groups.9 Of these proposals, 11 focused on a framework

for service during periods of insufficient resource adequacy while 13 were focused on the RBP

mechanism. Stakeholders made advisory votes on these proposals at the June 30, 2026 Special

Members Committee (“MC”) meeting, following the four-stage CIFP process which concluded

that same day. PJM also sought feedback from stakeholders on specific topics through further

polling, the results of which were finalized on July 10, 2026.10

        Based on these discussions that took place over eight stakeholder meetings between April

16 and June 30, 2026,11 and the results of the June 30, 2026 stakeholder advisory votes,12 the PJM

Board is currently deliberating on the final proposals that PJM will file with the Commission

regarding RBP and a framework for service during periods of insufficient resource adequacy. A

finalized RBP proposal is expected to be filed with the Commission on or around July 31, 2026,

with the goal of administering a reliability backstop procurement shortly after Commission

acceptance of the proposal. PJM intends to file a proposal related to a framework for service

                     ii. Large Load Customer Flexibility

        PJM’s large load customer flexibility initiative is also slated to address a Problem

Statement13 and Issue Charge14 related to large load customer flexibility,15 which was approved by

the Markets and Reliability Committee (“MRC”) on March 25, 2026.16 This stakeholder process

recognizes the critical need to explore customer flexibility solutions that would allow certain large

load customers to connect to the grid prior to completion of necessary transmission upgrades and

therefore seeks to develop the tools, processes, business rules, and regulatory changes required to

address large load customer flexibility, including load shed prioritization and allocation.17 In light

of the Commission’s Show Cause Order, PJM is considering whether to explore the matter raised

in this Problem Statement and Issue Charge as part of its response to the directives of that order.

        Specifically, PJM and stakeholders expect to develop an allocation framework whereby

                 b. Stakeholder Processes Aiming to Increase the Pace of Adding Generating
                    Capacity in the PJM Region
                       i. Increasing the Pace of Adding Generating Capacity Through Markets
                              1. Powering Reliability Through Market Design
            Following the PJM Board’s January 16, 2026 Decisional Letter on the CIFP for Large Load

Additions directing staff to undertake a holistic review of the PJM capacity market design and

investment incentives,20 PJM released a report on Powering Reliability Through Market Design.21

This report delineated three potential paths forward: (1) stabilizing PJM’s long-term market; (2)

allowing for differential reliability between regions within the PJM Region; and (3) pursuing a

transition from reliance on the Reliability Pricing Model (“RPM”) for resource adequacy to the

energy and Ancillary Services markets.22 The first solution path preserves the existing capacity

energy and Ancillary Services markets thereby reducing the region’s reliance on the capacity

market as only a backstop mechanism to promote forward bilateral energy contracts as the primary

hedging instrument for LSEs.25

                              2. Reserve Certainty Reforms

        As highlighted in PJM’s report, the RCSTF is developing enhancements to recalibrate

reserve products and update reserve demand curves to better account for ramping and uncertainty

and better align reserve pricing with operational practice.29 The PJM proposal put forward in the

RCSTF is designed to provide more efficient economic incentives through enhanced products for

resources participating in PJM’s Ancillary Services markets which should also help increase the

pace of adding new generating capacity to the PJM Region through improved market signals.

Stakeholder discussion of this issue at the RCSTF concluded on June 25 and voting concluded on

July 10.30 The proposal will be discussed at the August 24 MRC and voted on at the September

MRC, with a final vote scheduled to take place at the October MC.31 If a proposal is endorsed by

stakeholders, PJM plans to file that proposal with the Commission by the end of 2026.32

                        ii. Increasing the Pace of Adding Generating Capacity Through
                            Interconnection Reforms
                                1. Expedited Interconnection Track
           On June 9, 2026, the Commission issued an order accepting PJM’s proposed Expedited

Interconnection Track (“EIT”) proposal.33 In so doing, the Commission found that PJM’s proposal

“accomplishes the purposes of Order Nos. 2003 and 2023 by helping to ensure that interconnection

customers are able to interconnect to the transmission system in a reliable, efficient, transparent,

and timely manner” and that the “EIT proposal will help address PJM’s near-term resource

adequacy needs by establishing a separate, time-limited, expedited interconnection process for a

limited number of resources that are able to bring significant capacity onto the system in the near-

term.”34

           The Commission found that the eligibility requirements proposed “are tailored to

addressing near-term resource adequacy needs and appropriately limit EIT to capacity resources

that are more likely to timely contribute to meeting the region’s needs”35 thereby increasing the

pace of adding generating capacity in the PJM Region. The EIT was developed through the

Critical Issue Fast Path – Large Load Addition (“CIFP-LLA”) stakeholder process36 which

culminated in a Special MC meeting on November 19, 2025. During that process, PJM and

stakeholders proposed multiple packages that included concepts around an expedited

                             2. Expansion of Provisional Service

        PJM’s Interconnection Process Subcommittee (“IPS”) is currently exploring an issue

charge to expand provisional service by identifying under what circumstances generation projects

that advance to Phase III of a Cycle may be permitted to safely and reliably begin generating prior

to their completion of certain Cycle studies without impacting the timing or fundamentally altering

the Generation Interconnection Procedures.38 The IPS intends to report the final results of polling

related to this stakeholder effort to the Planning Committee in September 2026 for further

consideration.39 PJM is also assessing the impact of the Show Cause Order on this topic.

                             3. Interconnection Process Subcommittee

ongoing interconnection cycle-based study process which has already made large improvements

to increasing the pace of adding generating capacity. PJM posted Phase II of its System Impact

Study reports on June 5, 2026, and is currently in Transition Cycle 2 Phase III, which started on

July 8, 2026.40 This final phase is presently projected to culminate in the negotiation of final
